about_text: A lightweight pure-ARM64 native Android emulator for Windows. QEMU full-machine emulation of ARM64 hardware — APKs execute native ARM instructions, with no x86 images and no binary translation. Fully compatible with ARM-only apps, hardened/protected apps and finance apps. Multi-instance, key mapping, macros, hardware spoofing, full ADB compatibility. Zero ads, zero bundling, no silent upload.
hint_tap_adapter: e.g. tap-bridge (a TAP adapter is required for bridged mode)
hint_image_source: By default the source is Auto: every built-in source is tried in order with fallback (China: ghfast.top, hf-mirror.com; global: GitHub Releases, Hugging Face). Pin one source or set a custom URL in Settings > Global Settings > Image Source; package layout is <source>/aosp-11..15-arm64.zip. You can also use Import to add an image manually (zip or folder, ARM64 with image.json).

vt_guide_title: How to enable VT-x / AMD-V hardware virtualization
vt_guide_intro: This emulator virtualizes a complete ARM64 machine via QEMU. Enabling firmware virtualization (Intel VT-x / AMD-V) plus the Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) unlocks hardware-level acceleration; otherwise it automatically degrades to software emulation with a notice.
vt_guide_bios_ok: VT-x / AMD-V is already enabled in BIOS, no BIOS change is needed.
vt_guide_bios_title: Step 1: Enable VT-x / AMD-V in BIOS
vt_guide_step1: Reboot the PC and press the BIOS hotkey repeatedly at startup (see the table below).
vt_guide_step2: Open the Advanced / CPU Configuration menu.
vt_guide_step3: Set Intel Virtualization Technology (VT-x) or SVM Mode (AMD-V) to Enabled.
vt_guide_step4: Press F10 to save and exit, and wait for the reboot.
vt_guide_step5: Come back and press "Re-check" to confirm the status.
vt_guide_whpx_1: Open Control Panel -> Programs -> Turn Windows features on or off.
vt_guide_whpx_2: Check "Virtual Machine Platform" (Windows Hypervisor Platform), click OK and reboot.
vt_guide_whpx_3: If third-party antivirus provides "hardware virtualization protection", allow the virtual machine platform to run.
vt_guide_done: When finished, press "Re-check" below — the indicator turns green once hardware acceleration is active.

welcome_desc: A pure ARM64 native Android emulator for Windows: it virtualizes a complete ARM64 phone, runs APKs natively and supports multi-instance, ADB and device spoofing. Follow the three steps below to get started.
welcome_step1_desc: Pick an Android version plus CPU / memory / disk settings to create a virtual phone.
welcome_step2_desc: Press "Start" in the list; the display window opens automatically once it is running.
welcome_step3_desc: Drag & drop .apk files onto this window, or use "Install APK" in the toolbar.
welcome_hint: Tip: each instance exposes its own ADB port in the list — adb connect 127.0.0.1:<port> works with third-party tools and scripts.
qs_intro: StarARM is an Android emulator (native ARM64 emulation): create Android instances, install APKs, run multiple copies and automate them.
qs_step1_text: Press "New Instance" in the toolbar, choose a built-in Android 11-15 ARM64 image plus CPU / memory / disk settings. Clone, copy or export instances for multi-instance use.
qs_step2_title: Step 2: Boot and watch the screen
qs_step2_text: Press "Start"; the display window opens automatically when the state turns Running (press "Screen" to reopen it). Scaling, fullscreen, screenshot and recording are supported.
qs_step3_text: Three ways: drag .apk files onto the main window, press "Install APK" in the toolbar, or use the row menu "More -> Install APK". Multiple APKs can go to several running instances at once.
qs_step4_text: Every instance has its own ADB port (shown in the list) and works with adb connect and third-party tools. Key mapping, macros, device fingerprint & GPS spoofing, shared-folder sync, clone/backup and batch start/stop are supported.
